transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-18 15:00 PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Sam Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Tidal PM), Priya Kapoor (Tidal CTO), Nate Ruiz (Tidal Data Eng)

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex Morgan from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account, quick intros?
00:12 Jordan: Hey Jordan Lee, product at Tidal, thanks for doing this, excited.
00:18 Priya: Priya, CTO, I might jump in on infra questions.
00:22 Nate: Nate, I run the data pipelines and vector infra.
00:27 Sam: Sam Chen, systems engineer, I'll take the deeper infra questions.
00:33 Alex: Awesome, goal for today is to understand your current search architecture, what you want out of embeddings + rerank, and whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private makes sense. We'll also capture success criteria for a POC.
00:50 Jordan: Sounds good. Quick background: we have a product knowledge base + user-generated content, about 10M docs total but we'll start small for POC. Right now we use OpenSearch for BM25, evaluating Pinecone and Weaviate for vector search. We're struggling with hybrid search quality and latency at scale.
01:10 Alex: Helpful. When you say hybrid search, are you doing a BM25 candidate set + re-rank with embeddings, or some other pattern?
01:18 Nate: Yeah candidate set then similarity rerank. We tried approximate nearest neighbor straight to top-k but relevance dropped, so BM25 then embed rerank seems best.
01:30 Sam: Cool, that's a pattern we see a lot. A couple of knobs that matter: embedding dimensionality (e.g., 512 vs 1536), index type (HNSW, IVF), and whether the vector DB supports efficient batch rerank / nri--sorry I mean K/V cache and batching on our side.
01:50 Priya: Our latency target is p50 < 120ms for rerank across 10 candidate docs, p95 ideally < 300ms. Throughput needs are about 200 QPS for queries with rerank. Can Redwood meet that with Hosted or do we need Dedicated?
02:10 Sam: Great question. For p50 120ms on a 10-doc rerank at 200 QPS, Hosted might be fine initially but if you want consistent p95 and enterprise SLAs we'd recommend Dedicated — reserved GPU pools give predictable throughput. We can run a benchmark to validate.
02:30 Jordan: What about dimensionality — we already have embeddings at 768 from our vendor, but we see noisy signals. Is moving to 1536 worth the cost?
02:42 Alex: Tradeoffs: higher dimensional vectors can improve recall for complex semantics but increase storage and per-query compute. For many rerank flows with small candidate sets (10-50) going to 1536 has diminishing returns. Sam, do you want to add on runtime/quantization?
02:58 Sam: Sure. On Redwood runtime we support quantized execution paths and select kernels to optimize throughput; for rerank over 10-50 items the extra compute is small. The bigger impact is index size and memory on your vector DB — if you're self-hosting FAISS or Milvus, higher dims mean larger indexes and slower bulk ops. If you're using a managed vector DB with compression we can work with you.
03:18 Nate: We're leaning to keep 768 for now but curious if swapping models later is straightforward. Also curious about embedding serving vs storing precomputed vectors.
03:30 Alex: You can store precomputed vectors in your vector DB and call Redwood for rerank only, or call Redwood to generate embeddings via Hosted API and push to DB. For POC we usually ask customers to provide precomputed vectors to isolate retrieval/throughput variables.
03:48 Jordan: For vector DBs we've prototyped with Pinecone and a self-hosted FAISS cluster; Pinecone was easier but costs scaled. Have you seen customers plug Redwood into Pinecone?
03:58 Sam: Yes, many customers use Pinecone or Weaviate in front of their retrieval layer. Redwood acts as the rerank engine or the embedder depending on the flow. We have sample integrations and a benchmark template for Pinecone + Redwood rerank.
04:12 Priya: Security — we need SOC 2, SSO, KMS for key management and audit logs for inference. If we go Private, we need VPC peering or on-prem option. What does Redwood offer?
04:26 Alex: We support SOC 2, SAML SSO, KMS integrations and have Private deployments for VPC/on-prem with a customer-managed control plane. For Dedicated we offer private networking options too. We'll send the security pack after this call.
04:38 Nate: For POC we'd need to validate data handling — logs, retention, and whether embeddings are considered customer data.
04:45 Sam: We'll include data-handling specifics in the security docs. For Hosted by default we have opt-in retention policies; Dedicated and Private give you more control and isolation.
04:55 Jordan: OK good. Can we talk throughput numbers — like what hardware or concurrency do you typically provision for 200 QPS rerank?
05:05 Sam: For a 200 QPS rerank on 10 docs with a quantized model for rerank, you'd typically need a few GPUs if everything's colocated; but with efficient batching and concurrency the runtime can scale horizontally. On Dedicated we size clusters for predictable p95 targets; for Hosted we often throttle or route to fallback models under heavy load.
05:24 Priya: Do you provide an autoscaling policy for Dedicated? We want headroom for spikes up to 500 QPS.
05:31 Alex: Yes, Dedicated has configurable autoscaling and burst capacity. We'll put recommended policies in the proposal.
05:38 Jordan: About evaluation: we want to measure quality improvements vs cost delta. Typical metrics we care about are MRR increase after rerank and end-to-end latency. Is that what you recommend?
05:49 Sam: Exactly. For rerank we measure retrieval+rerank MRR or NDCG, plus latency percentiles. We can run an A/B on a 5k to 100k query set during POC.
06:00 Nate: For the data sample, can we keep doc size varied? We have 60% short docs (<200 tokens), 30% medium, 10% long. Also multi-language is a factor — English + Spanish.
06:15 Alex: That's fine. Our benchmark template includes distribution knobs; Sam will send it.
06:22 Jordan: Any limitations with hybrid search? We need smooth integration between OpenSearch candidate queries and vector DB. Does Redwood provide connectors or do we need to glue?
06:32 Sam: We have reference connectors and code snippets. Typical pattern: run BM25 in OpenSearch to get candidate IDs, fetch vectors from your vector DB by ID, then call Redwood for rerank. We can also host an end-to-end pipeline if you want less ops work.
06:48 Priya: If we go Private deployment, does the Redwood control plane still get telemetry? We are strict about PII and telemetry.
06:56 Alex: In Private, telemetry can be routed to your observability stack; we can disable certain telemetry. We'll include audit log capabilities and an enterprise agreement covering that.
07:06 Jordan: Good. Pricing rough ballpark? Need to evaluate Hosted per-token / embed cost vs Dedicated commit.
07:14 Alex: I'll send a pricing sheet. Ballpark — Hosted is usage-based and flexible; Dedicated is an ARR with reserved capacity which lowers unit cost. For your 200 QPS steady profile, Dedicated likely pays off after sustained usage.
07:29 Nate: For the POC, recommended duration and scope?
07:33 Sam: Usually a 2-4 week POC with 100k docs works well — covers ingestion, indexing, and a query workload to measure p50/p95 and quality. We'll also run throughput tests to validate autoscaling.
07:45 Jordan: That aligns. One question on rerank models — do you support custom rerank models or only standard cross-encoders?
07:55 Sam: We support multiple approaches: lightweight embedding-similarity rerank, cross-encoder rerank using fine-tuned models, and you can bring your own model artifacts for Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports selection from our curated model catalog.
08:12 Priya: For bringing models, what's the onboarding complexity?
08:17 Sam: For Dedicated/Private, we can load your model artifact; we have a model onboarding flow and template. For Hosted, model additions are managed by Redwood — we can discuss bringing a custom model under an enterprise agreement.
08:30 Jordan: Ok next, can you run a quick sketch of the POC workflow?
08:35 Alex: Sure: 1) Tidal provides anonymized 100k doc sample + query set, 2) Sam sends benchmark template and ingestion script, 3) Redwood runs benchmark on Hosted and Dedicated config, 4) compare MRR / latency / cost, 5) review results and decide next steps.
08:54 Jordan: Great. Any red flags we should expect?
08:58 Sam: The common issues are: unexpected index size with higher-dim vectors, candidate set quality from BM25, and network egress between vector DB and rerank engines if components aren't co-located. We'll help tune those.
09:12 Nate: For vector DB, do you have preference? We're inclined to stick with an existing FAISS cluster but open to Pinecone if ops cost is too high.
09:22 Alex: FAISS is cost-effective but ops heavy; Pinecone/Weaviate reduce ops but increase bills. Redwood integrates with both patterns. For Dedicated we can co-locate rerank to minimize cross-network cost.
09:35 Priya: Can the Redwood runtime do batching for rerank requests across customers? Any PII concerns?
09:43 Sam: Batching is per-tenant and respects isolation; for multi-tenant Hosted we have strong boundaries. For Private/Dedicated you get even stricter isolation.
09:53 Jordan: Great. Any recommended embedding dimension for a rerank-first approach? 768 seems fine?
09:58 Sam: Yes 512-1024 is often a good middle ground; 768 is widely used and fine for many workloads. If you plan to use very short texts, lower dims can be okay. For multilingual workloads consider models trained for multilingual embeddings.
10:15 Nate: How about caching? We have repeated similar queries and want to avoid regen.
10:20 Sam: Redwood supports prefix/KV caching; for rerank flows we cache embeddings and sometimes rerank outputs for high-frequency queries. We'll show configuration suggestions in the Optimize toolkit.
10:32 Jordan: What about evaluation metrics and dashboards, can we see per-route token cost and latency?
10:38 Alex: Redwood Console provides per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost, latency breakdowns, tracing and error analysis. We'll give demo access for the POC.
10:50 Priya: For the POC, we'd like to see both host and dedicated numbers so we can decide later.
10:56 Alex: Absolutely. We'll run both configurations and include cost estimates and suggested Dedicated sizing.
11:02 Jordan: Anything else on security? We need SOC 2 Type II evidence and an architecture whitepaper.
11:10 Alex: We'll attach SOC 2 docs and a Private deployment architecture whitepaper in the follow-up.
11:16 Nate: For ingestion, our docs are stored in S3 with metadata in Postgres. What's the best ingestion approach?
11:23 Sam: Use the ingestion script we'll share to batch extract, compute vectors (or use precomputed) and upsert to your vector DB. We also support incremental syncs for real-time updates.
11:36 Jordan: Are there constraints on document size for embeddings? We have some >5k token docs.
11:42 Sam: For very long docs you typically chunk and embed segments; Redwood supports chunking patterns and chunk-aware rerank.
11:50 Priya: One more infra ask — can you provide IPv4-based peering? Our VPC is on AWS and we need peering for Private.
11:58 Alex: Yes, Private supports AWS VPC peering and on-prem connectors. We'll document the network requirements.
12:06 Jordan: Ok wrapping up, can we recap next steps?
12:10 Alex: Sure. I'll send pricing + Dedicated proposal, Sam will share benchmark template and ingestion script, Nate will provide the anonymized data sample, and we'll aim to schedule the POC kickoff by next week.
12:24 Jordan: Sounds good. Thanks all.
12:27 Priya: Thanks everyone.
12:30 Alex: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs. End of call.
